stem: A company runs its web application on Amazon EC2 instances that use a Linux operating system the company chose. A new security patch for that operating system has been released. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, who must apply the patch?

choices.text: The company, because the guest operating system on an EC2 instance is part of what the customer configures and maintains.
Neither party, because EC2 instances are rebuilt from a fresh AWS image every night, which removes the need to patch them.
AWS, because every operating system running on AWS hardware is patched automatically during the scheduled host maintenance.
AWS and the company equally, because each patch must be approved by both parties before it can be applied to any instance.

stem: A company moves its self-managed MySQL database from an Amazon EC2 instance to Amazon RDS for MySQL. Which security task does the company no longer need to perform itself after the move?

choices.text: Deciding whether the database storage should be encrypted with an AWS KMS key.
Installing operating system and database engine patches on the database server.
Creating database user accounts and granting each account only the privileges it needs.
Configuring security group rules that limit which clients can reach the database port.

stem: A team deploys an application as AWS Lambda functions that use an AWS managed runtime. Under the shared responsibility model, which tasks are the team's responsibility? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Controlling physical access to the data centers that host the Lambda service fleet.
Patching the operating system of the servers that run the Lambda execution environments.
Applying security updates to the managed language runtime that executes the function.
Granting the function's execution role only the permissions the function actually needs.
Fixing security flaws in the function code and in the third-party libraries packaged with it.

stem: The AWS shared responsibility model describes some controls as "shared controls". Which example best matches a shared control?

choices.text: Destruction of failed storage devices, where AWS wipes and physically destroys drives before they leave a secure facility.
Physical and environmental protection, where the customer fully inherits the data center safeguards that AWS operates and audits.
Patch management, where AWS patches its infrastructure and the customer patches its own guest operating systems and applications.
Routing traffic between security zones inside a customer VPC, where only the customer designs and maintains the network layout.

stem: An external auditor asks a company for the AWS SOC 2 report and the AWS PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance to review how AWS secures its infrastructure. Where can the company download these documents?

choices.text: AWS Audit Manager, which collects evidence about the company's own AWS usage and maps it to compliance frameworks.
AWS Artifact, which offers on-demand access to AWS security and compliance reports and to select online agreements.
AWS Config, which records resource configurations over time and checks them against rules the company defines.
AWS Trusted Advisor, which inspects the company's account and recommends improvements for security and cost.

stem: An Amazon EC2 instance in a production account was terminated yesterday, and nobody admits to doing it. Which AWS service lets the administrator find which identity made the termination request and when?

choices.text: Amazon Inspector, which scans EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities and network exposure.
VPC Flow Logs, which capture information about IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in the VPC.
Amazon CloudWatch, which collects metrics such as CPU use and can raise alarms when a value crosses a threshold.
AWS CloudTrail, which records API calls in the account, including the caller identity, time and source IP address.

stem: A company's security policy says every Amazon EBS volume must be encrypted. The security team wants to be told automatically when a non-compliant volume appears and to see how each volume's settings have changed over time. Which AWS service meets these needs?

choices.text: AWS Config, using a rule that evaluates whether EBS volumes are encrypted and its record of configuration history.
Amazon Inspector, using its vulnerability scans to detect operating systems that were installed on unencrypted disks.
AWS Artifact, using its compliance reports to confirm that the EBS service supports encryption of all volumes.
AWS CloudTrail, using its record of API calls to list every volume that a user created in the account today.

stem: A healthcare company in Japan must keep patient records stored only in Japan and must encrypt them at rest. The records will be stored in Amazon S3. Which actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable AWS Shield Advanced on the bucket so the records are encrypted while they travel across the internet.
Put Amazon CloudFront in front of the bucket so the records are cached at edge locations near patients worldwide.
Configure the bucket's default encryption to use server-side encryption with an AWS KMS key that the company manages.
Download a Japanese compliance report from AWS Artifact, which then restricts all of the account's data to Japan.
Create the S3 bucket in an AWS Region located in Japan, because AWS does not move content out of the Region the customer chooses.

stem: A startup has just created a new AWS account using the founder's email address. Which action follows AWS best practices for protecting the root user?

choices.text: Create access keys for the root user so administrators can run automation scripts with full permissions from their laptops.
Keep using the root user for daily administration, but change its password every month and choose a longer passphrase.
Enable multi-factor authentication on the root user and use separate identities with limited permissions for everyday work.
Share the root user password with every administrator through a password manager so the account is never locked out.

stem: An application on an Amazon EC2 instance must read objects from one Amazon S3 bucket. The security team wants no long-term credentials stored on the instance and wants to follow least privilege. Which solution meets these requirements?

choices.text: Make the S3 bucket public so the application can read objects without needing any AWS credentials.
Generate access keys for the root user and pass them to the instance through environment variables at boot.
Create an IAM user with full S3 access and save its access keys in the application's configuration file.
Attach an IAM role to the instance with a policy that allows only reading objects from that one bucket.

stem: An administrator must give eight new IAM users in one AWS account the same set of permissions, and expects those permissions to change several times over the next year. What is the most manageable way to assign them?

choices.text: Create an IAM group, attach the required policies to the group, and add all eight users as members.
Create one shared IAM user for the team and give its password to all eight people who need the access.
Add the eight users to the account's root user so they inherit its permissions while their work is reviewed.
Attach a separate copy of the same inline policy to each of the eight users and edit every copy on change.

stem: A company has 30 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. Employees should sign in once with their existing corporate identity provider and then reach only the accounts and permissions their job needs. Which AWS service is designed for this?

choices.text: IAM users created separately in each of the 30 accounts, with the same user names and passwords in every account.
AWS IAM Identity Center, which connects to the identity provider and assigns permission sets to users for each account.
Amazon Cognito user pools, which let customers of a web or mobile app sign up and sign in with social identity providers.
AWS Directory Service, which runs managed Microsoft Active Directory domain controllers for Windows workloads in a VPC.

stem: A security team sees malicious traffic coming from one specific IP address and wants to block that address from reaching every instance in a subnet. Which control can do this directly?

choices.text: An IAM policy with an explicit deny for that IP address, attached to the subnet so the address cannot send traffic to it.
A network ACL on the subnet with a deny rule for that IP address, since network ACLs support both allow and deny rules.
A route table entry that sends the attacker's IP address to the internet gateway, so its packets are returned unanswered.
A security group on each instance with a deny rule for that IP address, since security groups evaluate deny rules first.

stem: A public web application runs behind an Application Load Balancer. Logs show SQL injection attempts, and the company also wants enhanced DDoS protection with access to an AWS response team during attacks. Which services should the company use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: AWS WAF, with rules that inspect web requests and block common SQL injection patterns.
Amazon GuardDuty, which analyzes account logs to find compromised instances and credentials.
AWS Secrets Manager, which stores database passwords and rotates them on a regular schedule.
Amazon Macie, which discovers and reports sensitive data such as personal information in S3.
AWS Shield Advanced, which adds DDoS detection, mitigation and Shield Response Team support.

stem: A security team wants a managed service that continuously analyzes AWS CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs and DNS query logs to detect threats such as compromised credentials or instances communicating with known malicious IP addresses. Which service should the team enable?

choices.text: Amazon Inspector, which scans EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for known software vulnerabilities.
Amazon Detective, which builds graphs from collected logs to help analysts investigate the root cause of a finding.
Amazon GuardDuty, which uses threat intelligence and machine learning on account and network activity to produce findings.
Amazon Macie, which uses machine learning and pattern matching to find sensitive data stored in Amazon S3 buckets.

stem: A company must create the same network, servers and database in three AWS accounts. It wants the setup described in version-controlled files so every environment is built identically and can be updated or deleted as one unit. Which AWS service meets this need?

choices.text: AWS Elastic Beanstalk, which deploys uploaded application code and automatically handles capacity, load balancing and platform updates.
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, which opens browser-based shell sessions to each server so administrators can run setup steps.
AWS Config, which records the configuration of each resource and evaluates it against rules to report resources that drift from policy.
AWS CloudFormation, which provisions the resources declared in a template as a stack that can be updated, rolled back or deleted together.

stem: A manufacturer transfers several terabytes from its data center to AWS every night. Transfers over its internet link are slow and unpredictable. It wants a private, dedicated connection with consistent network performance that does not use the public internet. What should it use?

choices.text: AWS Site-to-Site VPN, which creates encrypted IPsec tunnels between the data center router and a virtual private gateway over the internet.
AWS Global Accelerator, which routes user traffic to applications through static anycast IPs at AWS edge locations.
AWS Direct Connect, which links the data center to AWS through a dedicated network connection at a Direct Connect location.
AWS Client VPN, which lets each employee's laptop connect to the VPC through an encrypted OpenVPN-based tunnel over the internet.

stem: A film studio in Los Angeles runs graphics workstations that need single-digit millisecond latency to compute in AWS. The nearest AWS Region is too far away, and the studio does not want to install or operate any hardware itself. Which option fits best?

choices.text: AWS Local Zones, which place AWS compute, storage and selected services in a large metropolitan area close to the users there.
Amazon CloudFront edge locations, which cache and deliver static and dynamic web content from points close to viewers worldwide.
AWS Outposts, which installs AWS-managed racks of compute and storage in the customer's own data center or office building.
AWS Wavelength Zones, which place AWS compute inside telecommunications carriers' 5G networks for applications serving mobile devices.

stem: A European company is choosing the AWS Region for a new customer-facing application. Which TWO factors should most directly influence the choice? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The number of CloudFront edge locations inside the Region, because CloudFront serves content only from edge locations in the origin's Region.
The distance between the Region and most of the application's users, because shorter distance means lower latency.
The number of Availability Zones in the Region, because service level agreements apply only to Regions with at least four zones.
The Region in which the AWS account was first created, because resources can later be launched only in that Region.
Laws or contracts that require customer data to be stored within a specific country or jurisdiction.

stem: A hospital must process patient imaging data inside its own building because of local data residency rules and very low latency needs to on-site equipment. It wants to use the same AWS services, APIs and tools it uses in the cloud. Which AWS offering meets these needs?

choices.text: AWS Storage Gateway, which gives on-premises applications access to cloud storage through a local cache appliance.
AWS Local Zones, which run AWS compute in an AWS-operated facility in a nearby metropolitan area connected to a parent Region.
AWS Direct Connect, which provides a dedicated private network link between the hospital and the nearest AWS Region.
AWS Outposts, which delivers AWS-designed infrastructure that AWS installs and manages inside the customer's own facility.

stem: Each time a user uploads a photo to an Amazon S3 bucket, a company needs to create a thumbnail. Each job takes about two seconds, uploads are irregular, and the company wants to pay nothing while no photos arrive. Which compute option is the best fit?

choices.text: An AWS Lambda function that S3 invokes for each new object, billed only for the requests and the time the code runs.
An Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance with a one-year term that processes the photos in a scheduled batch every night.
An Amazon ECS service on an EC2 cluster that keeps two container tasks running and polls the bucket for new photos.
An Amazon EC2 On-Demand instance that runs all day and checks the bucket every minute for new photos to process.

stem: A team packages its application as Docker containers. It wants to run them on AWS without provisioning, patching or scaling any EC2 instances for the cluster. Which option meets this requirement?

choices.text: Amazon EKS with self-managed nodes, which runs Kubernetes pods on EC2 worker instances the team launches and updates.
Amazon Elastic Container Registry, which stores, versions and scans the team's container images in a private repository.
Amazon ECS with the EC2 launch type, which places containers on EC2 instances that the team registers to the cluster.
Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate, which runs each task on compute that AWS provisions and manages behind the scenes.

stem: A web application on Amazon EC2 has heavy traffic during business hours and very little at night. The company wants to add and remove instances automatically with demand and spread requests across healthy instances in several Availability Zones. Which TWO services should it use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Amazon CloudWatch dashboards, to display CPU and request graphs so operators can see when to resize instances.
Elastic Load Balancing, to distribute incoming requests across the healthy instances in multiple Availability Zones.
Amazon EBS snapshots, to copy the instance volumes to Amazon S3 so new instances start from a saved image.
Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts, to place all instances on physical servers reserved for the company's use only.
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, to launch and terminate instances in a group based on demand or a schedule.

stem: A gaming company needs a database to store player profiles and session data as key-value items. It must return results in single-digit milliseconds at any scale, and the company does not want to manage servers or database instances. Which service should it choose?

choices.text: Amazon Redshift, a columnar data warehouse that runs complex analytical SQL queries across large historical datasets.
Amazon RDS for MySQL, a managed relational engine that runs on a database instance size the company selects and scales.
Amazon DynamoDB, a serverless NoSQL key-value and document database that scales throughput automatically on demand.
Amazon Neptune, a managed graph database designed for querying relationships between highly connected data items.

stem: A company wants to move its on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The source database must keep serving users during the move, with only a short cutover at the end. Which AWS service is designed for this?

choices.text: AWS Database Migration Service, which converts schemas and replicates data, including ongoing changes, to the target.
AWS Application Migration Service, which replicates whole servers to Amazon EC2 so they run unchanged in AWS.
AWS Storage Gateway, which connects on-premises applications to cloud storage through a locally cached virtual appliance.
AWS DataSync, which copies files and objects between on-premises storage and AWS storage services on a schedule.

stem: A company serves product images and videos from an Amazon S3 bucket in one Region. Customers on other continents report slow load times. The company wants to cache this content close to viewers worldwide with minimal changes. Which service should it use?

choices.text: Amazon S3 Express One Zone, which gives very low latency storage in a single Availability Zone in one Region.
Amazon CloudFront, which caches the content at edge locations and serves each viewer from a nearby location.
AWS Global Accelerator, which routes viewer traffic over the AWS global network through two static anycast IP addresses.
S3 Cross-Region Replication, which keeps full copies of every object in buckets in other Regions automatically.

stem: In an Amazon VPC, a solutions architect is asked what makes one of the subnets a public subnet. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Its instances use a security group that allows inbound traffic on all ports from the source range 0.0.0.0/0.
Its CIDR block is taken from a public IP range instead of a private range such as 10.0.0.0/8 or 192.168.0.0/16.
Its route table sends traffic for addresses outside the VPC to a NAT gateway placed in another subnet of the VPC.
Its route table has a route that sends traffic for addresses outside the VPC to an internet gateway attached to the VPC.

stem: A company stores millions of objects in Amazon S3. Some are read daily, others go untouched for months, and nobody can predict which. The company wants to lower storage costs automatically without retrieval fees or lifecycle rules to maintain. Which storage class fits best?

choices.text: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access, which stores data in a single Availability Zone at a lower price than Standard-IA.
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, which has a very low storage price but requires a restore job before an object can be read.
S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which monitors access and moves each object between access tiers based on how often it is read.
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access, which has a lower storage price but charges a retrieval fee for each GB that is read.

stem: A company runs a content management system on 12 Linux EC2 instances spread across three Availability Zones. All instances must read and write the same files at the same time through a standard file system, and storage should grow automatically. Which storage service should it use?

choices.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, which provides a managed SMB file share integrated with Microsoft Active Directory.
Amazon EC2 instance store, which provides temporary block storage on disks physically attached to the instance's host.
Amazon EBS General Purpose volumes, which provide block storage that is attached to an instance in the same Availability Zone.
Amazon EFS, which provides a managed NFS file system that many instances in multiple Availability Zones can mount at once.

stem: A news website wants to add two features: reading articles aloud to visitors in a natural-sounding voice, and a chatbot that understands typed or spoken questions about subscriptions. Which TWO AWS services should it use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Amazon Transcribe, to convert the article text into audio files.
Amazon Lex, to build the conversational chatbot interface.
Amazon Rekognition, to read article text aloud to visitors.
Amazon Comprehend, to hold conversations with site visitors.
Amazon Polly, to convert the article text into lifelike speech.

stem: A security team keeps months of application log files in Amazon S3. Analysts occasionally need to run standard SQL queries against these files without loading them into a database or managing any servers. Which service should they use?

choices.text: Amazon Athena, which runs SQL queries directly against the data in S3 and charges for the amount of data each query scans.
Amazon Redshift provisioned clusters, which run complex analytical SQL queries on data that is first loaded into the cluster.
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, which collects records in real time from many producers so consumer applications can process them.
AWS Glue ETL jobs, which run serverless Spark scripts to clean, transform and move data between data stores on a schedule.

stem: An online store's order service sends each new order directly to a fulfillment service. During sales the fulfillment service is overwhelmed and orders are lost. The company wants orders held safely until the fulfillment service can process them at its own pace. Which service should it place between them?

choices.text: Amazon CloudWatch, which collects metrics and logs from both services and raises alarms when error rates increase.
Amazon SNS, which pushes each published message right away to every subscribed endpoint, such as email, SMS or HTTPS.
Amazon SQS, which stores messages in a queue until a consumer retrieves, processes and deletes each one.
AWS Step Functions Express Workflows, which run short, high-volume workflows that last at most five minutes each.

stem: An online education startup based in Canada signs a contract with a university in Japan and must serve students there with low latency within two weeks. The startup has no staff or offices in Asia. Which benefit of the AWS Cloud makes this practical?

choices.text: Massive economies of scale, because AWS buys hardware in bulk and passes the lower unit cost on to every customer through lower prices.
Stop guessing capacity, because Auto Scaling in the startup's current Region adds servers automatically when Japanese students log in.
Go global in minutes, because the startup can deploy its application in an AWS Region near Japan without building any facilities there.
Trade fixed expense for variable expense, because the startup pays for servers in Japan only during the hours that students are online.

stem: A ticketing company runs its website in its own data center. Traffic is ten times higher during the few days a year when concert sales open, so the company buys servers for that peak, and they sit mostly idle the rest of the year. Which AWS Cloud benefit addresses this problem most directly?

choices.text: Go global in minutes, because the company can copy its website to Regions on several continents and spread the concert traffic among them.
Stop guessing capacity, because the company can add servers when sales open and remove them afterward, paying only while they run.
Increase speed and agility, because developers can launch new test environments in minutes instead of waiting weeks for new hardware orders.
Benefit from massive economies of scale, because AWS buys hardware in bulk and lowers prices for all of its customers over time.

stem: A company's IT team spends most of its week replacing failed disks and patching hypervisors, and new projects wait eight weeks for servers to be ordered and installed. Which TWO AWS Cloud benefits address these problems? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers, because AWS handles the physical hardware so staff can focus on applications.
Free licensing for all commercial software, because every instance price already includes licenses for any database the team installs.
Guaranteed capacity in every Availability Zone, because AWS reserves spare instances for each account without any commitment or fee.
Shift all security responsibility to AWS, because AWS patches customer applications and configures user permissions in each account.
Increase speed and agility, because teams can provision new resources in minutes through the console or API instead of waiting for hardware.

stem: An architect reviews a workload against the AWS Well-Architected Framework. The design should recover automatically when a component fails, and the team should regularly test its recovery procedures. Which pillar do these design principles belong to?

choices.text: Operational excellence, which focuses on running workloads effectively, gaining insight into operations and improving processes over time.
Performance efficiency, which focuses on using computing resources efficiently and keeping that efficiency as demand and technology change.
Sustainability, which focuses on reducing the environmental impact of workloads by maximizing utilization and choosing efficient resources.
Reliability, which focuses on a workload performing its intended function correctly and consistently, and recovering quickly from failures.

stem: A development team ships one large release every quarter. Each release changes hundreds of components at once, and when something breaks it is hard to find the cause and roll back. Which Well-Architected design principle should the team adopt?

choices.text: Make frequent, small, reversible changes, so each deployment touches few components and can be rolled back easily if it fails.
Scale horizontally to increase aggregate availability, so that the failure of one large server no longer affects the entire workload.
Use serverless architectures, so the team no longer has to run servers and AWS manages capacity for each function automatically.
Analyze and attribute expenditure, so the team can see which components and projects are responsible for the workload's costs.

stem: A team wants to answer a structured set of questions about one of its workloads, compare the answers with AWS best practices across all six pillars, and get a list of high-risk issues with improvement plans. Which AWS resource should the team use?

choices.text: AWS Compute Optimizer, which analyzes resource utilization metrics and recommends better instance types and sizes for running workloads.
AWS Config conformance packs, which evaluate resource configurations against a collection of rules and report which resources are noncompliant.
AWS Well-Architected Tool, which guides a workload review against the framework's pillars and records the risks and improvement plans found.
AWS Trusted Advisor, which runs automated checks on the resources in the account and recommends fixes for cost, security, and service quotas.

stem: A company must leave its data center in four months when the lease ends. It runs 60 applications on virtual machines, and there is no time to change application code. Which migration strategy fits most of these applications?

choices.text: Repurchase, replacing each application with a software as a service product and moving the existing data into the new product.
Refactor, rebuilding the applications as cloud-native services to gain scalability and agility from managed and serverless features.
Replatform, moving each application while swapping parts such as its database for a managed service with a few small optimizations.
Rehost, moving each server as it is to Amazon EC2 so the applications run on AWS quickly without changing their code.

stem: A bank is planning its cloud adoption with the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF). Leaders worry that staff lack cloud skills, that job roles will need to change, and that teams may resist new ways of working. Which AWS CAF perspective addresses these concerns?

choices.text: Operations perspective, which ensures cloud services are delivered at a level that meets the needs of the business, with monitoring and incident management.
People perspective, which serves as a bridge between technology and business, focusing on culture, organizational structure, leadership, and workforce.
Business perspective, which ensures cloud investments accelerate digital transformation and support the organization's business outcomes and strategy.
Governance perspective, which orchestrates cloud initiatives while maximizing organizational benefits and minimizing transformation-related risks.

stem: A company plans to migrate 40 on-premises application servers to Amazon EC2 and its Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, keeping downtime short during cutover. Which TWO AWS services should it use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: AWS Application Migration Service, which continuously replicates the source servers and launches them as Amazon EC2 instances at cutover.
AWS Transfer Family, which provides SFTP endpoints so the database administrators can upload nightly export files into the cloud.
AWS Storage Gateway, which presents cloud storage as local volumes so the existing servers can keep running from the data center.
AWS DataSync, which copies the virtual machine disk images into Amazon S3 so they can be started as instances in a later step.
AWS Database Migration Service, which copies the data and keeps it in sync, with DMS Schema Conversion to convert the Oracle schema.

stem: A finance director asks how moving workloads from the company's data center to AWS will change the way IT costs appear in the budget. Which statement best describes the change?

choices.text: Capital and operating expenses both stay the same, because AWS bills customers for a fixed number of servers on a yearly contract.
Operating expenses disappear, because AWS includes all compute, storage, and data transfer in one flat monthly fee for each account.
Large up-front capital expenses for hardware are replaced by variable operating expenses that follow actual usage of AWS resources.
Variable operating expenses are replaced by a single large capital expense, because AWS requires payment for three years of service up front.

stem: A company is building a total cost of ownership (TCO) comparison between its on-premises environment and AWS. The draft lists only the purchase price of its servers on the on-premises side. Which additional costs should be added to make the comparison fair?

choices.text: The AWS Support plan fees, AWS Marketplace subscriptions, and training costs, which apply only after the move and belong only on the AWS side.
The price of the AWS Free Tier offers and of the services AWS includes at no charge, valued at their normal On-Demand rates.
The costs of application licenses and developer salaries only, because these are the only costs that differ between the two environments.
The power, cooling, floor space, network hardware, and staff time needed to install, maintain, and replace the on-premises hardware.

stem: A company moving to AWS owns licenses for database software that are priced per physical CPU socket and core, and it wants to reuse them instead of buying new licenses. Which Amazon EC2 option supports this bring-your-own-license (BYOL) approach?

choices.text: Spot Instances, which use spare EC2 capacity at a steep discount and include the database licenses in the hourly price.
Dedicated Hosts, which give the company a physical server and visibility into its sockets and cores for license counting.
Dedicated Instances, which run on hardware dedicated to one customer but do not show which physical sockets and cores the instances use.
On-Demand Instances with license-included pricing, which charges for the database license as part of each running hour.

stem: A media company runs a nightly video transcoding job that can be stopped and restarted at any time without losing work, and the deadline is flexible. The company wants the lowest possible compute cost. Which EC2 purchasing option should it use?

choices.text: Reserved Instances, which give a discount in exchange for a one-year or three-year commitment to a specific instance configuration.
Spot Instances, which use spare EC2 capacity at a large discount and can be interrupted by AWS with a two-minute warning.
On-Demand Instances, which charge by the second with no commitment and are not interrupted by AWS to reclaim spare capacity.
Dedicated Hosts, which give the company an entire physical server for its own use and visibility into the server's sockets and cores.

stem: A company has steady compute usage that it expects to keep for three years. Over that time it plans to change EC2 instance families, move between Regions, and run part of the workload on AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda. Which pricing model gives a discount while allowing all of these changes?

choices.text: Spot Instances, which offer the deepest discount on spare capacity and apply automatically to Fargate tasks and Lambda functions too.
Standard Reserved Instances, which offer a large discount for a specific instance type in a Region and cannot be exchanged for a different family.
EC2 Instance Savings Plans, which offer one of the largest discounts in exchange for committing to one instance family in one chosen Region.
Compute Savings Plans, which apply a lower rate to EC2 usage in any family, size, or Region and to Fargate and Lambda usage as well.

stem: Several project teams share one AWS account. Finance wants to see monthly costs broken down by project in AWS Cost Explorer. Every resource already carries a `Project` tag, but Cost Explorer cannot group costs by it. What should the company do?

choices.text: Move each project's resources into its own Availability Zone, so Cost Explorer can group the costs of each project by Availability Zone.
Create an AWS Budgets cost budget for each project, which automatically adds a project grouping column to every report in Cost Explorer.
Activate `Project` as a user-defined cost allocation tag in the Billing and Cost Management console, then group by it in Cost Explorer.
Run AWS Pricing Calculator estimates for each project and upload them into Cost Explorer as the monthly cost breakdown.

stem: A company with 15 AWS accounts, each paying its own bill, plans to bring them into AWS Organizations and turn on consolidated billing. Which TWO benefits will it gain? (Select TWO)

choices.text: One bill paid by the management account, with the charges of each member account still shown separately in the billing data.
The IAM users of all member accounts are merged into the management account so they sign in with a single set of credentials.
Member accounts are blocked automatically from spending more than their share of the monthly bill set by the management account.
Every member account receives the features of a paid AWS Support plan at no extra cost once it joins the organization.
Usage from all accounts is combined for tiered volume pricing, and Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts can be shared.

stem: An operations team wants to be notified when AWS plans scheduled maintenance that will affect the specific EC2 instances in its account, and wants to see which of its resources are affected by an ongoing AWS service issue. Which AWS resource provides this?

choices.text: AWS Config, which records configuration changes to resources over time and evaluates them against rules that the team defines.
AWS Health Dashboard, which shows AWS events affecting the account's resources, such as scheduled maintenance and service issues.
AWS CloudTrail, which records the API calls made in the account, including who made each call, when it was made, and from where.
AWS Trusted Advisor, which checks the account against best practices and flags issues such as idle resources and open security groups.

stem: A company wants to use a third-party log analytics product on AWS. It wants to subscribe to it, deploy it into its own account, and have the software charges appear on its existing AWS bill instead of signing a separate contract with the vendor. Where should it look?

choices.text: AWS Marketplace, a curated catalog where customers find, subscribe to, and deploy third-party software with charges billed through AWS.
AWS Service Catalog, which lets administrators publish a set of approved products that users in their organization can launch.
AWS re:Post, a community question-and-answer site where AWS customers, partners, and AWS experts answer technical questions.
AWS Partner Solutions Finder, which helps customers search for AWS Partners that offer consulting services and solutions.

stem: An administrator adds a custom network ACL to a public subnet. Its inbound rules allow HTTPS on port 443 from anywhere, and it has no outbound rules other than the default deny. The instance's security group allows inbound 443. Users can no longer load the website. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Network ACL rules apply only to traffic between subnets, so internet traffic must be allowed in the route table.
The security group is stateless, so it must also have an outbound rule that allows responses on port 443 to clients.
The network ACL is stateless, so it must also allow the outbound response traffic to the clients' ephemeral ports.
A network ACL cannot be used together with a security group, so the security group rules are now being ignored.

stem: A bank's security standard says IAM user passwords must have at least 14 characters, include numbers and symbols, expire after 90 days and not reuse recent passwords. How can the bank enforce these rules for its IAM users?

choices.text: Create an AWS Config rule that checks password strength, which blocks IAM users from choosing a weak password.
Store every IAM user's password in AWS Secrets Manager and turn on automatic rotation every 90 days for each user.
Attach a service control policy to the account that lists the minimum password length and complexity required.
Set an IAM account password policy with the required length, character types, expiration and reuse prevention.

stem: A developer at a gaming studio accidentally pushed an IAM user's access key ID and secret access key to a public code repository. What should the studio do first?

choices.text: Deactivate the exposed access key, then replace it with a new one and review CloudTrail for unauthorized activity.
Enable MFA on the IAM user, because API calls signed with access keys then require an MFA code to succeed.
Change the IAM user's console password, because a new password also invalidates any access keys that the user owns.
Make the repository private, because removing public access to the file stops anyone from using the copied keys.

stem: A data analytics company still uses IAM user access keys for several scripts. Which practices reduce the risk from these long-term credentials? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create root user access keys as a backup in case an IAM user's access key stops working unexpectedly.
Replace access keys with IAM roles and temporary credentials wherever the workload can assume a role.
Embed the keys in the script source code so they are versioned and backed up with the repository.
Share one IAM user's access key among all scripts so there are fewer keys to track in the account.
Rotate the keys that must remain on a regular schedule and remove keys that are no longer used.

stem: An application on AWS Lambda connects to an Amazon RDS database. The security team wants the database password removed from the code and changed automatically on a schedule. Which service meets these requirements?

choices.text: AWS Secrets Manager, which stores the password encrypted and can rotate it automatically on a schedule.
IAM access keys created for the Lambda function, which replace the database password for RDS connections.
Amazon S3 with default encryption, where the function reads the password from a private object at start-up.
AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS), which stores the password as a key and rotates it every year.

stem: A company uses AWS IAM Identity Center to give employees access to its AWS accounts. What defines the level of access, such as read-only or administrator, that a user receives in an assigned account?

choices.text: A service control policy, which grants employees permissions in member accounts once they sign in to the portal.
A permission set, a template of policies that Identity Center provisions as an IAM role in each assigned account.
An IAM group created separately in every account, to which the administrator adds each employee's IAM user by hand.
A security group attached to the access portal, which allows or denies the employee's traffic into each account.

stem: A small architecture firm with one AWS account is setting up access for its 12 employees. Which approach does AWS recommend for these human users?

choices.text: Create one IAM user per employee with long-term access keys for the CLI and a password for the console.
Have all employees sign in as the root user with MFA so that every action uses the same audited identity.
Federate employees through an identity provider, such as IAM Identity Center, so they use temporary credentials.
Create a single shared IAM user with administrator permissions and store its password in a team vault.

stem: An IAM user at a travel agency belongs to a group whose policy allows all Amazon S3 actions. A second policy attached directly to the user explicitly denies s3:DeleteObject. What happens when the user tries to delete an object?

choices.text: The delete is denied, because a user who belongs to a group cannot also have policies attached directly to it.
The delete succeeds, because the group policy allows all S3 actions and group policies take precedence over user policies.
The delete succeeds, because AWS applies whichever policy was attached most recently to the user or to the group.
The delete is denied, because an explicit deny in any applicable policy overrides any allow from other policies.

stem: In an IAM policy statement, which element lists the API operations, such as s3:GetObject or ec2:StartInstances, that the statement allows or denies?

choices.text: The Effect element, which lists each operation that the statement covers with its permission setting.
The Condition element, which names the operations along with the circumstances under which they apply.
The Action element, which names the service prefix and the operations that the statement covers.
The Resource element, which names the operations that may be performed on the listed resource ARNs.

stem: A nonprofit needs to give its volunteers view-only access to its AWS account today. It has no IAM expertise and wants the permissions kept up to date as AWS releases new services. Which type of policy fits best?

choices.text: A customer managed policy written from scratch, which the nonprofit must update itself whenever new services are added.
An inline policy embedded in each volunteer's IAM identity, which is deleted automatically when that identity is deleted.
A service control policy in AWS Organizations, which grants view-only permissions to every principal in the account.
An AWS managed policy for the job function, which AWS creates and updates when new services and actions are added.

stem: Which statement best describes how an IAM role differs from an IAM user?

choices.text: A role can be used only by AWS services, while a user can be used by people, applications and AWS services alike.
A role has no long-term password or access keys; trusted entities assume it and receive temporary credentials.
A role is a collection of IAM users that share one password, while a user is an individual identity with its own password.
A role always has full administrator permissions, while a user has only the permissions attached to it directly.

stem: An administrator is writing identity-based policies in IAM. Besides IAM users, which identities can these policies be attached to? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An IAM role that applications or other accounts assume to get permissions.
An AWS KMS key that encrypts the data the administrator's team stores in AWS.
An Amazon S3 bucket that stores the reports the administrator's team works with.
An Amazon VPC subnet that hosts the instances the administrator's team manages.
An IAM group that holds several IAM users who need the same permissions.

stem: An e-commerce company runs an order service on AWS Lambda. The function must write to an Amazon DynamoDB table and call a third-party payment API that requires an API key. Which steps follow AWS access best practices? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Store the payment API key in AWS Secrets Manager and let the function's role read only that secret.
Attach the AdministratorAccess policy to the function so it never fails because a permission is missing.
Write the payment API key into the function code so it ships with every deployment of the package.
Create an IAM user for the function and put its access keys in the function's environment variables.
Give the function an execution role whose policy allows writing only to the one DynamoDB table it uses.

stem: A healthcare startup with several AWS accounts in AWS Organizations wants continuous findings for IAM roles that have not been used recently and for permissions that roles and users hold but never use. Which capability is designed for this?

choices.text: Amazon GuardDuty, which reports any IAM role that has been inactive for 90 days as a high-severity threat finding.
IAM Access Analyzer unused access findings, which report unused roles, access keys, passwords and permissions.
The IAM credential report, which lists each role's unused permissions and is refreshed every hour for all member accounts.
AWS Config, which deletes IAM roles automatically once they reach a set number of days without any recorded activity.

stem: A logistics company is writing a Python application that must upload delivery photos to Amazon S3 and write tracking records to Amazon DynamoDB as part of its normal code. Which way of interacting with AWS fits this best?

choices.text: AWS CloudFormation, which declares the S3 bucket and the DynamoDB table in a template and creates them together as one stack.
The AWS Console Mobile Application, which lets staff view resources and perform selected tasks from a phone while away from a desk.
An AWS SDK for Python (Boto3), which lets the application code call the S3 and DynamoDB APIs directly with signed requests.
The AWS Management Console, where an operator opens the S3 and DynamoDB pages and adds each photo and record through the web forms.

stem: A software team wants to define its AWS infrastructure in TypeScript, the language it already uses, so it can use loops, classes and its usual code editor to build many similar resources. The result should still be deployed as CloudFormation stacks. Which service should it use?

choices.text: AWS CloudFormation StackSets, which deploy one existing CloudFormation template to many AWS accounts and Regions in one operation.
AWS Elastic Beanstalk, which takes the team's application code and deploys it on a managed platform with capacity and load balancing.
AWS Systems Manager, which runs commands and automation documents across fleets of instances to configure them after launch.
AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK), which turns infrastructure code written in common programming languages into CloudFormation templates.

stem: An operations team does most of its AWS work in the Management Console. Which TWO tasks would benefit most from being moved into infrastructure as code templates? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Browsing the list of instance types once to compare memory sizes while drafting an early design for a new project.
Creating an identical test environment for every release branch and removing it after testing ends a few days later.
Opening the billing dashboard once to check whether last month's charges look reasonable before a budget meeting.
Viewing a single CloudWatch graph once to see how CPU use changed during an incident that happened earlier today.
Keeping a standby copy of the production environment in a second Region that must match production after every change.

stem: An insurance company has 300 employees working from home on their own internet connections. They need secure access to internal applications that run on private IP addresses in an Amazon VPC. Which AWS service meets this need?

choices.text: AWS Direct Connect, which provides a dedicated physical link from a colocation facility to AWS that bypasses the public internet.
VPC peering, which connects two Amazon VPCs so their resources can reach each other using private IP addresses.
AWS Client VPN, a managed service that lets each user's device open an encrypted VPN session into the VPC over the internet.
AWS Site-to-Site VPN, which connects an on-premises network router to a virtual private gateway or transit gateway with two IPsec tunnels.

stem: A retail chain is starting a three-month pilot that sends small amounts of sales data from one store's network to an Amazon VPC. The link must be encrypted, working within a day, and cheap. Which connectivity option fits best?

choices.text: An internet gateway in the VPC, which lets the store's servers send the sales data to public IP addresses of the VPC instances.
AWS Client VPN, which installs a VPN client on each store employee's laptop so every person opens a tunnel into the VPC.
AWS Direct Connect, which orders a dedicated private circuit from the store's network to a Direct Connect location near the Region.
AWS Site-to-Site VPN, which builds encrypted IPsec tunnels between the store's router and AWS over the store's existing internet link.

stem: A manufacturing company keeps its plant-floor control systems in its own data center, runs its new online ordering website on AWS, and connects the two so orders flow to the plant. Which cloud deployment model is this?

choices.text: A hybrid deployment, because workloads run both on premises and in the AWS Cloud and the two environments are connected.
A cloud (all-in) deployment, because the online ordering website and its data run entirely on AWS managed services.
A multi-Region deployment, because the company uses more than one physical location to run its business applications.
An on-premises (private cloud) deployment, because the plant control systems stay on servers in the company's own data center.

stem: A national research agency runs all of its applications on servers it owns in its own facility. It uses virtualization and a self-service portal so teams can request virtual machines, and it uses no public cloud provider. Which deployment model describes this setup?

choices.text: An edge deployment, because the applications run at a location close to the researchers instead of in a provider's data center.
A hybrid deployment, because the agency's self-service portal gives teams a cloud-like experience for requesting new virtual machines.
An on-premises deployment, also called a private cloud, because all resources run on the agency's own hardware in its own facility.
A cloud deployment, because teams can create virtual machines on demand without waiting for new physical servers to be purchased.

stem: A new cloud engineer asks how the AWS Management Console, the AWS CLI and the AWS SDKs differ in the way they reach AWS services. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The Management Console changes resources directly on AWS hardware, so its actions are not recorded by AWS CloudTrail as API calls.
The SDKs can only be used by code that runs on Amazon EC2, while the CLI is required for any automation from outside AWS.
The CLI and SDKs bypass IAM policies because they use access keys, while only the Management Console checks user permissions.
All three send authenticated requests to the AWS service APIs, so IAM permissions apply the same way whichever tool is used.

stem: An administrator sees five EC2 instances in the Europe (Ireland) Region in the Management Console. Running `aws ec2 describe-instances` in the AWS CLI on a laptop with valid credentials for the same account returns an empty list. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The CLI default Region on the laptop is different from Europe (Ireland), so the command lists instances in another Region.
The AWS CLI can list only instances that were launched with the CLI, so instances created in the console never appear in its output.
The instances are in the stopped state, and the CLI returns only running instances unless a special license is enabled.
The IAM user needs a separate CLI access policy, because console permissions do not include the right to call EC2 APIs.

stem: An auditor working on a locked-down laptop that does not allow software installs needs to run a few AWS CLI commands against the company's account. Which option lets the auditor do this from a web browser with no setup?

choices.text: AWS Elastic Beanstalk, which creates an EC2 environment with a preinstalled platform where the auditor can upload command scripts.
AWS CloudShell, a browser-based shell opened from the Management Console with the AWS CLI already installed and the user's credentials.
The AWS Console Mobile Application, which shows resources and selected actions on a phone without installing tools on a laptop.
AWS Systems Manager Run Command, which runs scripts on registered EC2 instances and on-premises servers through the Systems Manager agent.

stem: A company is building a hybrid architecture and must connect its entire on-premises corporate network to an Amazon VPC so that servers in both locations can communicate privately. Which TWO AWS options can provide this network-to-network connection? (Select TWO)

choices.text: AWS Site-to-Site VPN, which links the corporate network's VPN device to AWS through encrypted IPsec tunnels over the internet.
An internet gateway, which attaches to the VPC so that instances with public IP addresses can send and receive internet traffic.
AWS Client VPN, which gives each employee's laptop its own encrypted session into the VPC from any internet connection.
Amazon CloudFront, which delivers the company's web content to users through a worldwide network of edge locations.
AWS Direct Connect, which links the corporate network to AWS through a dedicated private connection at a Direct Connect location.

stem: A student preparing for a cloud certification asks what an AWS Availability Zone is. Which description is correct?

choices.text: An AWS-managed rack of servers installed in a customer's own building that connects back to a parent Region for management.
A worldwide site where Amazon CloudFront caches copies of content so that viewers in nearby cities receive it with lower latency.
One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking and connectivity, physically separated from others in a Region.
A geographic area such as a country or large metro area that contains several fully independent AWS Regions for data residency.

stem: An online pharmacy runs its web application on four Amazon EC2 instances, all in one Availability Zone, behind an Application Load Balancer. A power problem in that zone took the whole site offline for two hours. What change would best prevent this kind of outage?

choices.text: Replace the four instances with two larger instance types in the same Availability Zone so each instance has more spare capacity.
Add Amazon CloudFront in front of the load balancer so that edge locations keep serving the dynamic pages when the origin fails.
Move all four instances into a cluster placement group in the same Availability Zone so they share faster networking hardware.
Spread the instances across at least two Availability Zones in the Region and have the load balancer route to healthy ones.

stem: A payment processor already runs across three Availability Zones. Its regulator now requires a plan to restore service if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable. Which TWO actions support this disaster recovery requirement? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add a fourth Availability Zone in the same Region to the load balancer so that traffic can be shifted to more locations.
Copy Amazon EBS snapshots and Amazon Machine Images on a regular schedule to a second AWS Region so servers can be rebuilt there.
Turn on Amazon RDS Multi-AZ so a standby database in another Availability Zone of the same Region takes over automatically.
Increase the size of the EC2 Auto Scaling group so it keeps more instances running across the existing three zones.
Enable Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication so new objects are copied automatically to a bucket in a different AWS Region.

stem: A company learns that AWS edge locations are far more numerous than AWS Regions. Which TWO AWS services use edge locations to serve their customers? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Amazon CloudFront, which caches and delivers web content and APIs to viewers from locations close to them around the world.
Amazon EFS, which provides a shared file system for instances that is stored redundantly across zones of one Region.
Amazon EBS, which provides block storage volumes attached to EC2 instances within a single Availability Zone of a Region.
Amazon RDS, which runs managed relational database instances in subnets inside Availability Zones of a chosen Region.
Amazon Route 53, which answers DNS queries for a company's domain names from a worldwide network of servers.

stem: A sports broadcaster is building an augmented reality app for fans in the stadium. The app runs on phones connected to a mobile carrier's 5G network and needs ultra-low latency to the game-state servers. Which AWS infrastructure option fits this best?

choices.text: AWS Local Zones, which place AWS compute and storage in a large metropolitan area for users who connect through ordinary networks there.
AWS Outposts, which deliver AWS-managed racks to the broadcaster's own facility so the servers can run inside its building.
AWS Wavelength Zones, which place AWS compute and storage inside a telecommunications carrier's 5G network at the edge.
Amazon CloudFront edge locations, which cache the app's static files close to fans in cities around the world for faster downloads.

stem: A developer in a company that uses a newer AWS Region cannot find a recently launched AWS service in the Management Console, although a colleague using a different Region sees it. What is the most likely reason?

choices.text: The console caches its service list for each browser, so the developer must clear the browser history before new services appear.
The service is offered only to accounts that have purchased Reserved Instances, so it stays hidden until a commitment is made.
The developer's IAM user lacks permission to view the service, because AWS hides services from users who cannot use them.
The service is not yet available in the developer's Region, because new services and features are rolled out to Regions over time.

stem: A research lab runs large overnight batch simulations on Amazon EC2. Results are downloaded the next morning, the data has no residency rules, and nobody needs fast interactive responses. The required services exist in every Region it considers. Which factor should most influence its Region choice?

choices.text: The distance to the lab's researchers, because the lowest possible latency is always the most important factor for any workload.
The price of the needed EC2 instances and storage, because prices for the same resources can differ from one AWS Region to another.
The Region the lab's AWS account was created in, because an account's resources must all run in that original home Region.
The number of CloudFront edge locations in each country, because batch output can only be downloaded through the nearest edge.

stem: A legal firm stores client contracts in an Amazon S3 bucket in the Europe (Paris) Region. A partner asks whether AWS might move or copy those files to another Region for its own operational reasons. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: S3 data is stored at edge locations worldwide by default, so copies of the contracts exist wherever CloudFront has an edge location.
AWS automatically copies all S3 data to at least one other Region on the same continent to protect it against Region-wide outages.
Data stays in the Region where the customer stores it, and it moves to another Region only if the customer copies or replicates it.
AWS moves data between Regions when one Region is busy, so the customer cannot guarantee where the contracts are stored at a given time.

stem: A gaming company in Dallas plans to use an AWS Local Zone for low-latency game servers. A teammate asks how a Local Zone relates to the rest of AWS. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: A Local Zone is a separate, independent Region with its own full set of AWS services, IAM users and a separate billing account.
A Local Zone is an extension of a parent Region; you enable it and create a subnet there in a VPC that belongs to that Region.
A Local Zone is a group of CloudFront edge locations that can also run EC2 instances when content caching capacity is unused.
A Local Zone is AWS hardware installed in the customer's own data center that the customer orders, powers and connects locally.

stem: An administrator switches the Management Console from US East (N. Virginia) to Asia Pacific (Seoul). The EC2 instances she created disappear from view, but all IAM users and roles still appear. What explains this?

choices.text: The administrator lacks permission to view EC2 in Seoul, because EC2 permissions are granted Region by Region in the console.
IAM data is copied to each Region once a day, while EC2 instances are copied only when cross-Region replication is enabled.
The EC2 instances were deleted when the console Region changed, while IAM users are protected from deletion by a default policy.
EC2 instances are Regional resources shown only in their own Region, while IAM is a global service that is the same in all Regions.

stem: An online travel booking site has large customer groups in Western Europe and Southeast Asia. Users in Asia complain that pages generated from the single Europe-based deployment are slow, and the data has no residency limits. Which approach best reduces latency for both groups?

choices.text: Deploy the application in a Region near each group and use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to send users to the nearest one.
Move the whole application to a Region halfway between the two groups so that each group is roughly the same distance away.
Upgrade the European EC2 instances to larger sizes so that each page is generated faster and the distance matters less.
Add more Availability Zones to the existing European deployment so that Asian users have more data centers to connect to.

stem: An online retailer discovers that customer invoices stored in an Amazon S3 bucket were downloaded by strangers. Investigation shows an employee had turned off S3 Block Public Access and added a bucket policy that allows public reads. Under the shared responsibility model, whose responsibility was this exposure?

choices.text: AWS's, because Amazon S3 is a fully managed service, so AWS must review every new bucket policy before it takes effect on stored objects.
AWS's, because S3 should reject any bucket policy that grants public read access to objects that contain personal information.
Both equally, because access to S3 objects is a shared control that AWS and the customer must approve together for each bucket.
The retailer's, because deciding who can read objects, through bucket policies and Block Public Access settings, is security in the cloud.

stem: A company encrypted its Amazon S3 objects with a customer managed key in AWS KMS. An administrator scheduled the key for deletion, the waiting period ended, and now the objects cannot be decrypted. The company opens a support case asking AWS to restore the key. What is the expected outcome?

choices.text: AWS cannot restore it, because the key lifecycle, including deletion of a customer managed key, is the customer's responsibility and the deletion is final.
AWS restores it after verifying account ownership, because AWS keeps a recovery copy of each deleted customer managed key for one more year.
AWS decrypts the objects with its own master key instead, because S3 always keeps a second encrypted copy of each object under an AWS owned key.
AWS restores it from its own backup of KMS key material, because AWS is responsible for the durability of every key stored in the KMS service.

stem: A logistics company runs its containers on Amazon ECS with a cluster of EC2 instances that it manages. It plans to switch the same tasks to AWS Fargate. Which security task moves from the company to AWS after the switch?

choices.text: Scanning the company's own container images for vulnerable software packages before deploy.
Writing the IAM task role policies that decide which AWS resources each task may call.
Patching the operating system and container agent on the hosts that run the containers.
Choosing which ports the tasks' security groups allow from the company's load balancer.

stem: A school district is learning which parts of security AWS handles for workloads that run on Amazon EC2. Which items are AWS responsibilities under the shared responsibility model? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Installing TLS certificates on the district's web servers so that student logins are encrypted.
Maintaining the routers, switches and fiber links that connect AWS data centers and Regions.
Configuring the firewall software running inside the guest operating system of each instance.
Writing the security group rules that decide which traffic can reach the district's instances.
Providing power, cooling and fire suppression in the facilities that host the EC2 servers.

stem: A financial analytics firm runs sensitive calculations on Amazon EC2. Its risk officer worries that another AWS customer whose instances run on the same physical server could read the firm's instance memory. Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for preventing that?

choices.text: The firm, because it must install memory encryption software in each guest operating system to block other tenants on that host.
The other customer, because each tenant must sign an agreement with AWS that forbids reading memory owned by neighboring tenants.
AWS, because isolating instances from each other through the hypervisor and host hardware is part of security of the cloud.
The firm, because it must add security group rules that deny all traffic coming from other AWS customers' instances on the host.

stem: A design agency stores client artwork in Amazon S3. Which tasks are the agency's responsibility under the shared responsibility model? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Turning on S3 Versioning if the agency wants to recover files that staff overwrite or delete by mistake.
Destroying old storage media before it leaves the AWS data center so that deleted artwork cannot be read again.
Replacing failed disks in the S3 storage fleet so that the stored artwork files remain durable over time.
Applying security patches to the servers and software that run the Amazon S3 service in each Region.
Classifying which artwork files are confidential and deciding who in the agency may access each bucket.

stem: A company stores documents in Amazon S3. Which statement about encryption at rest best fits the shared responsibility model?

choices.text: The company must encrypt every object in its own application before upload, because Amazon S3 stores all objects without any encryption at rest at all.
AWS encrypts objects only when the company signs a separate data protection addendum, because encryption at rest is outside the standard S3 service.
AWS selects the most suitable encryption key type for each object automatically, so the company has no encryption decisions left to make for its bucket.
AWS supplies the encryption features and encrypts new objects with SSE-S3 by default, and the company decides if it needs another option such as SSE-KMS.

stem: A travel booking company uses Amazon Aurora MySQL for its reservations database. Which task does AWS perform for the company under the shared responsibility model?

choices.text: Deciding which VPC security groups and subnets may send connections to the cluster's endpoint and database port.
Detecting and repairing failed storage segments in the cluster volume that is spread across Availability Zones.
Choosing whether to encrypt the cluster with an AWS KMS key when the database cluster is being created.
Creating database accounts for each booking application and granting each account only the privileges it needs.

stem: A compliance team is mapping its controls to the AWS shared responsibility model. Which controls does AWS describe as shared controls? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Configuration management, where AWS configures its infrastructure devices and the customer configures its own guest operating systems, databases and applications.
Service and communications protection, where the customer routes and segments its own data into security zones inside its environment.
Host isolation on shared servers, where the hypervisor keeps one customer's virtual machines separated from other customers' instances.
Physical and environmental protection, where the customer relies fully on the safeguards that AWS builds and audits in every data center.
Awareness and training, where AWS trains AWS employees and the customer trains its own employees on how to use and secure its workloads.

stem: A payments startup is preparing for an audit of its workloads that run on Amazon EC2. Its auditor asks which controls the startup can document as fully inherited from AWS, with no action required by the startup. Which control fits?

choices.text: Reviewing every quarter which IAM users and roles can stop, start or terminate the startup's EC2 instances.
Applying operating system patches to the instances in a monthly maintenance window that the startup has chosen.
Hardening the configuration of each instance's guest operating system against the startup's security baseline.
Physical and environmental controls of the data centers, such as access badges, guards, power and climate control.

stem: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which example is a customer-specific control, one that AWS has no part in for the customer's workload?

choices.text: Media sanitization, where storage devices are wiped and destroyed before they leave the secured AWS data center sites.
Zone security, where the customer segments its own VPC into tiers and routes data between them according to its own rules.
Awareness and training, where both AWS and the customer make sure their own staff understand secure cloud practices.
Patch management, where updates are applied to infrastructure by AWS and to guest systems by the customer for each service.

stem: A game studio's Amazon EC2 instance was taken over by attackers. The security group allowed SSH on port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, and the Linux user had a weak password. The studio asks why AWS did not prevent the attack. Which explanation is correct?

choices.text: AWS should have rejected the weak password, because AWS enforces password strength for every user account inside guest operating systems.
The studio's ISP is responsible, because security for internet traffic arriving at a VPC belongs to the provider that delivers it.
Security group rules and operating system credentials are customer configuration, so securing them is the studio's responsibility.
AWS should have blocked the traffic, because AWS is responsible for filtering all attack traffic before it reaches any EC2 instance.

stem: A developer at a marketing agency pushed an IAM user's access key to a public code repository. Within hours, unknown parties used the key to launch resources in the agency's account. Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for protecting that access key?

choices.text: The code hosting provider, because it accepted the file and is responsible for preventing secrets in its repositories from being used.
AWS, because IAM is a global service and global services fall entirely under security of the cloud in the shared responsibility model.
AWS, because AWS issues every access key and must therefore detect and block any request made with a key that has been leaked.
The agency, because managing IAM credentials, including storing, rotating and revoking access keys, is the customer's responsibility.

stem: A small nonprofit with no operations staff is building a donation API. It wants to keep its share of security work under the shared responsibility model as small as possible. Which design meets this goal best?

choices.text: Amazon ECS on a cluster of EC2 instances that the nonprofit manages, running both the API container and a database container.
Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions and Amazon DynamoDB tables, so no servers or operating systems exist for it to manage.
Amazon EC2 instances behind a load balancer and Amazon RDS for the database, so only the web tier's operating system is its job.
Amazon EC2 instances running a web server and a database the nonprofit installs, with patches applied by a scheduled script.

stem: A research lab must run a custom kernel module and a specialized monitoring agent inside the operating system of its compute servers. It is choosing between Amazon EC2 and AWS Lambda. Which statement describes the trade-off under the shared responsibility model?

choices.text: Lambda gives the lab root access to the execution environment for kernel modules, and AWS still keeps full responsibility for patching it.
EC2 and Lambda carry the same customer responsibilities, because the shared responsibility model applies equally to every AWS compute service.
EC2 gives the lab the operating system access it needs, but the lab then becomes responsible for patching and hardening that operating system.
EC2 moves operating system patching to AWS once a custom kernel module is installed, because AWS must then certify the modified kernel.

stem: An insurance company in Germany must keep customer data inside the European Union. It plans to store the data in Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB. Under the shared responsibility model, who decides in which geographic location the data is stored?

choices.text: The company, because it picks the AWS Regions, and AWS keeps content in them except as the customer directs or the law requires.
The local regulator, because European authorities assign each company an approved AWS Region when it registers to process personal data.
AWS, because AWS places each customer's data in the Region with the most spare capacity and moves it between continents to balance usage.
AWS, because AWS determines the customer's legal obligations from its billing address and stores data in a Region that satisfies those laws.

stem: A media company runs Kubernetes workloads on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with worker nodes in EKS managed node groups of EC2 instances in its own account. Which task is AWS's responsibility?

choices.text: Scanning the container images that the teams deploy for vulnerable libraries before they run in production.
Updating the worker nodes to newer Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) that contain the latest operating system patches.
Configuring Kubernetes role-based access control so that each team can deploy only to its own namespaces.
Operating, scaling and patching the Kubernetes control plane, including the API server and its etcd data store.
