stem: A travel agency runs its booking site in one AWS Region and keeps a static "we will be back soon" page in Amazon S3 in another Region. When the main site stops responding, users should be sent to the backup page automatically. Which Route 53 feature meets this need?

choices.text: Simple routing with both addresses in one record, so client browsers pick one of them at random each time they connect.
Failover routing with a health check on the main site, so DNS answers switch to the backup page when the check fails.
Geoproximity routing with a bias toward the main site, so users are drawn to whichever site lies closest to their location.
Weighted routing with equal weights on both records, so half of all users always reach the backup page during normal operation.

stem: An online multiplayer game uses UDP and runs on servers in two AWS Regions. Players' home routers and corporate firewalls must allow a fixed set of IP addresses, and traffic should move to the healthy Region within seconds if one fails. Which service fits best?

choices.text: Elastic Load Balancing with an Application Load Balancer, which spreads HTTP and HTTPS requests over targets in one Region.
Amazon CloudFront, which caches game assets at edge locations and serves each player's HTTP requests from a nearby location.
AWS Global Accelerator, which gives two static anycast IP addresses and routes TCP and UDP traffic to healthy Regional endpoints.
Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing, which returns DNS answers that point each player to the closest Region it measures.

stem: A retail group has 35 VPCs across several accounts in one Region and a Site-to-Site VPN to its head office. Managing dozens of one-to-one connections between VPCs has become error-prone. It wants one central hub that connects all VPCs and the VPN. Which service fits best?

choices.text: VPC peering, which creates a private connection between two VPCs and must be set up separately for every pair that talks.
AWS PrivateLink, which exposes one specific service in a VPC to consumers through interface endpoints in their own VPCs.
An internet gateway, which connects each VPC to the internet so the VPCs and the office can reach each other over the internet.
AWS Transit Gateway, which acts as a regional hub that VPCs and VPN connections attach to and route traffic through.

stem: A university connects its research VPC to a shared-services VPC with VPC peering, and the shared-services VPC is also peered with a library VPC. Researchers find that instances in the research VPC cannot reach the library VPC. What is the reason?

choices.text: VPC peering is not transitive, so traffic cannot pass through the shared-services VPC to reach a VPC peered only with it.
VPC peering connections work only between VPCs in the same AWS account, so the library VPC must be moved into the research account.
VPC peering requires an internet gateway in every VPC involved, and the shared-services VPC does not have one attached yet.
VPC peering carries only IPv6 traffic between VPCs, so the IPv4 instances in each VPC must first be given IPv6 addresses.

stem: A logistics company runs batch jobs on EC2 instances in a private subnet. The jobs read and write large files in Amazon S3. The company wants this traffic to stay on the AWS network without going through a NAT gateway or the internet. What should it use?

choices.text: A gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3, added as a target in the private subnet's route table for S3 traffic.
An internet gateway attached to the VPC, with S3 traffic from the private subnet routed through it directly.
S3 Transfer Acceleration, enabled on the bucket so uploads enter AWS through the nearest CloudFront edge location.
AWS Direct Connect, ordered from the VPC to a Direct Connect location close to the AWS Region of the S3 bucket.

stem: A payments SaaS provider wants hundreds of customers to call its API from their own VPCs using private IP addresses. It must not open its VPC to customers' networks or deal with overlapping IP ranges. Which AWS capability is designed for this?

choices.text: AWS Transit Gateway shared with every customer account, with each customer VPC attached to the provider's hub.
VPC peering between the provider's VPC and each customer's VPC, with routes to the API servers added on both sides.
AWS PrivateLink, with the API published as an endpoint service that customers reach through interface endpoints.
AWS Site-to-Site VPN from each customer VPC to the provider's VPC, with tunnels terminated on a virtual private gateway.

stem: A logistics company runs an SFTP server on one EC2 instance in a public subnet. A partner's firewall accepts only IP addresses, but the server's public IPv4 address changes whenever the instance is stopped and started. What is the simplest fix?

choices.text: Turn on auto-assign public IPv4 for the subnet, so the instance receives the same public address from AWS each time it is started.
Create a Route 53 record for the instance, so the partner's firewall rule can use the server's domain name instead of its address.
Place a NAT gateway in the public subnet, so the partner's connections arrive at the instance through the NAT gateway's fixed address.
Allocate an Elastic IP address and associate it with the instance, so the same public IPv4 address stays with it across stops and starts.

stem: A developer launches a web server on EC2 in a public subnet whose route table already sends `0.0.0.0/0` to an internet gateway, but users cannot load the site over HTTPS from the internet. Which TWO issues could cause this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The subnet has no NAT gateway, which every instance needs before it can accept connections arriving from the internet.
The instance's security group has no inbound rule that allows TCP port 443 from the internet address range.
The instance is not registered in AWS Transit Gateway, which provides the path between public subnets and the internet.
The VPC has no gateway endpoint for Amazon S3, which is required for any instance to answer requests on the internet.
The instance has no public IPv4 address or Elastic IP address, so the internet has no address it can use to reach it.

stem: A startup that is new to AWS asks what Amazon Route 53 can do for its website, beyond answering DNS queries for its domain. Which TWO capabilities does Route 53 provide? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Caching copies of the website's images and pages at edge locations so that distant visitors receive them faster.
Registering new domain names, such as the startup's own .com name, and renewing them, all from within the AWS account.
Issuing and renewing public TLS certificates for the domain so that the website can serve its pages over HTTPS.
Inspecting web requests and blocking SQL injection and cross-site scripting attempts before they reach the website.
Checking the health of the website's endpoints and sending DNS answers only to endpoints that are currently healthy.

stem: A recipe website runs on EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer in one Region. Its pages, photos and videos are viewed worldwide. The company plans to put Amazon CloudFront in front of the load balancer. Which TWO benefits will this bring? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The VPC will no longer need security groups, because CloudFront filters every request before it can reach the instances.
Photos and videos will be stored permanently at the edge, so the copies at the origin can be deleted to cut storage costs.
The website's EC2 instances and database will be copied automatically to every AWS Region where viewers are located.
Cached copies of photos and videos at edge locations will let distant viewers load them with lower latency.
Requests answered from the edge caches will no longer reach the load balancer and instances, which reduces their load.

stem: A data analyst stored intermediate results on the local disk of an EC2 instance. After the instance was stopped overnight to save costs and started again, the files were gone, although the boot volume was intact. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.text: The files were on an instance store volume, which loses its data when the instance is stopped, hibernated or terminated.
The files were in Amazon S3, and S3 removes objects automatically when the instance that uploaded them is stopped.
The files were on an Amazon EFS file system, and EFS deletes files when the last instance that mounted it is stopped.
The files were on an Amazon EBS volume, and EBS volumes are erased each time the instance that they are attached to is stopped.

stem: An engineer needs to move the data on an Amazon EBS volume in Availability Zone A to a new EC2 instance in Availability Zone B of the same Region. EBS volumes cannot be attached across zones. What is the standard way to do this?

choices.text: Turn on EBS Multi-Attach for the volume, so the instance in Availability Zone B can mount it alongside the original one.
Change the volume's Availability Zone setting in the console, which moves the volume while it stays attached to the instance.
Create a snapshot of the volume, then create a new volume from that snapshot in Availability Zone B and attach it there.
Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication on the volume, so its blocks are copied automatically to Availability Zone B.

stem: A media company writes application logs to Amazon S3. Logs are read often in the first 30 days, rarely for the next year, and must then be deleted. The company wants this handled automatically without moving objects by hand. What should it configure?

choices.text: S3 Versioning on the bucket, which keeps every earlier version of each log and removes older versions after one year.
S3 Cross-Region Replication to a second bucket, which stores the replicated logs in a cheaper Region after 30 days.
An S3 Lifecycle configuration that transitions logs to a cheaper storage class after 30 days and expires them later.
S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket, which uploads new logs through edge locations to reduce the cost of storing them.

stem: Employees of an architecture firm sometimes overwrite or delete drawings stored in an Amazon S3 bucket by mistake. The firm wants to be able to restore the earlier version of any drawing after such an accident. Which S3 feature should it enable?

choices.text: S3 Transfer Acceleration, which routes each upload through an edge location so that the drawings arrive at the bucket faster.
S3 Inventory, which produces a scheduled report listing the objects in the bucket together with their size and metadata.
S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which moves each drawing between access tiers automatically depending on how often it is read.
S3 Versioning, which keeps every version of an object so an earlier version can be retrieved after an overwrite or delete.

stem: A bank must keep scanned loan documents for ten years for regulators. The documents are almost never read, and if an auditor requests one, waiting up to 48 hours is acceptable. The bank wants the lowest possible storage cost in Amazon S3. Which storage class fits best?

choices.text: S3 Glacier Deep Archive, which offers the lowest-cost S3 storage for long-term archives restored within about 12 to 48 hours.
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, which offers low-cost archive storage with retrieval in milliseconds for data read about once a quarter.
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access, which offers lower-cost storage with millisecond access for data read less than once a month.
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, which offers archive storage with restores that complete in minutes to hours after a request.

stem: A radiology clinic keeps older X-ray images in Amazon S3. Each image is opened only a few times a year, but when a doctor needs one it must appear in milliseconds. The data must survive the loss of an Availability Zone. Which storage class is most cost-effective?

choices.text: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, which charges less to store the images but returns each one only after a restore job finishes.
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, which charges a low archive storage price yet returns each image in milliseconds when read.
S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access, which charges less to store the images by keeping a single copy set in one Availability Zone.
S3 Glacier Deep Archive, which charges the least to store the images but returns each one only hours after it is requested.

stem: A law firm is moving its Windows-based document management application to AWS. The application stores files on SMB shares, uses NTFS permissions and requires integration with the firm's Microsoft Active Directory. Which managed service fits best?

choices.text: Amazon S3, which provides fully managed object storage in buckets that applications access through S3 REST API calls.
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, which provides fully managed Windows file shares over SMB integrated with Active Directory.
Amazon EFS, which provides a fully managed elastic NFS file system that Linux-based instances can mount from several zones.
Amazon FSx for Lustre, which provides a fully managed high-performance file system for compute-intensive workloads like HPC.

services: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

stem: A genomics research team runs short jobs on hundreds of EC2 instances. The jobs need a shared file system with very high throughput and sub-millisecond latency, and the input data already sits in an Amazon S3 bucket. Which storage service is designed for this?

choices.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, which offers managed SMB file shares with Active Directory integration for office users.
AWS Storage Gateway S3 File Gateway, which offers on-premises servers NFS and SMB access to S3 through a local cache.
Amazon FSx for Lustre, which offers a high-performance parallel file system that can be linked to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, which offers low-cost archive storage for data restored in minutes to hours when needed.

stem: A manufacturer's on-premises backup software writes to a physical tape library. The company wants to stop buying and storing tapes offsite but keep using the same backup software and process. Which AWS service supports this?

choices.text: AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway, which presents a virtual tape library to the backup software and stores the tapes in AWS.
AWS DataSync, which runs scheduled online transfers that copy files from on-premises file shares into AWS storage services.
Amazon EBS snapshots, which create point-in-time copies of block volumes that are attached to instances inside the VPC.
Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, which provides managed NetApp file systems with NFS, SMB and iSCSI access in a VPC.

stem: A company runs workloads that use Amazon EBS, Amazon RDS, Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon EFS across 20 accounts in AWS Organizations. Auditors want one place to define backup schedules and retention and to report on backup compliance. Which service fits best?

choices.text: AWS Config, which records the configuration of resources over time and evaluates them against compliance rules.
Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager, which automates the creation, retention and deletion of EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs.
Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication, which copies new objects from a source bucket into a bucket in a second AWS Region.
AWS Backup, which applies central backup plans to many AWS services and accounts and reports on backup activity.

stem: A team that is new to AWS is comparing Amazon EBS with Amazon S3 for a project. Which TWO statements correctly describe Amazon EBS? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An EBS volume is created in one Availability Zone and is attached to EC2 instances in that same zone.
An EBS volume grows and shrinks automatically as files are written and deleted, with no size set in advance.
An EBS volume is reached directly from any web browser through a unique HTTPS URL for each stored file.
An EBS volume automatically keeps copies in every AWS Region so the data survives the loss of a whole Region.
An EBS volume keeps its data when the instance it is attached to is stopped, because it persists separately.

stem: A marketing agency plans to store campaign images and videos in Amazon S3. Its staff are used to traditional file servers. Which TWO statements about Amazon S3 are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Each bucket must be given a fixed storage capacity when it is created, and the bucket rejects uploads once that capacity is full.
Changing part of an object is done by writing only the changed bytes, in place, as with a file opened on a local disk drive.
Each bucket is mounted as a block device that EC2 instances format with a file system and use as their operating system boot disk.
Data is stored as objects in buckets, and each object is identified by a key and holds the data together with its metadata.
Storage is virtually unlimited, and the agency pays for the data it actually stores rather than for capacity provisioned in advance.
